description.purpose: Deterministic screening on an ingress channel, as topology: one code cell and one rule store between the surface and the agent. Every inbound turn is measured -- size, sender, forbidden literal, rate -- and leaves on exactly one of two lanes: 'pass' with the body byte-identical, or 'reject' naming the reason AND the rule that fired. Nothing here asks a model, and nothing here can: every verdict is a comparison or a clock. The rule set lives in rows, so a colony shows its screening policy as part of its tree and changes it with an insert.
description.use_when: In front of every inbound channel -- Telegram, Slack, HTTP, voice -- wherever a stranger can reach the surface. Instantiate it in the SAME mutation that wires the ingress lane and both exits: the surface into ./screen with hop.route 'in_turn' and the channel identity promoted to context.channel (and context.user_id where the surface has one), ./screen out on hop.route=='pass' into the agent's intake, and ./screen out on hop.route=='reject' into a drain or a log. Both exit edges MUST delete the firewall's context keys (fw_body, fw_now, fw_phase, store_origin), otherwise the parked copy of the turn rides along downstream.
description.not_in_scope: No answer to the sender: the firewall never speaks outbound, and what a reject becomes -- a drain, a log line, a polite refusal, a ban -- is the parent tree's decision. No model judgement of any kind, not for classification and not for phrasing. No regex engine: a pattern rule is a case-folded substring or prefix literal. No secret handling, no auth, no session: the firewall knows a channel and a user id, nothing about who they are. No pruning of the arrivals ledger and no deletion of a rule -- disabling a row is the retraction.
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty since GH #228; an edge naming ./screen is refused with hive_port_boundary). Entry: the parent edge names the lane with set_hop route 'in_turn' and promotes the identity to context.channel / context.user_id; optionally hop.recorded_at stamps the turn from outside. Exits (on hop.route, both leaving the hive path, both clearing the firewall's own context keys inside): 'pass' -> the agent's intake, body unchanged; 'reject' -> a drain or log sink, carrying hop.reject_reason and hop.rule_id.

RULE ORDER, first match decides: (1) size cap FIREWALL_MAX_CHARS, arithmetic, before the first store hop; (2) an unreadable rule row -- fail closed, the row is named; (3) sender blocklist; (4) sender allowlist, per dimension, an empty allowlist admits everything; (5) pattern blocklist, substring then prefix; (6) rate limit LAST, because it is the only rule that consumes budget.
a fresh instance with the shipped seed: five example rows, all enabled 0 -- the row-driven rules ship inert, the two arithmetic rules (size, rate) are live from the first turn

closing a channel to everyone but one caller: two inserts into rules (kind sender, action allow, field channel / field user_id) and the next turn is already screened against them -- no restart, no code change

a blocked pattern demonstrably never reaches the agent: the reject lane leaves ./screen, the pass lane is the ONLY edge into the intake, and the rejected turn is on the hop with the rule_id that fired
